# the contributor audit: directional shape, retained endpoint credit, and relocation



The first-coordinate conditional transport is genuinely comonotone in the selected scalar projection. The full map still supplies the previously audited density bound and exact vector midpoint mean. The inverse of a decreasing concave bijection is concave with the direction of the displayed inequality; inversion again proves upper-tail root concavity. Reversal uses the same scalar coupling, so both tails belong to the same eta_u. The source vector is independent of u even though the measures need not be. The text correctly prohibits summing these different measures as one common law.

The unused-endpoint identity is pointwise and retains one actual tilt. Its indicator error is zero or one, including closed boundaries. Quantile equality is restricted to proper cuts; the event identity survives every saturated status. The centroid tail estimate follows from Jensen applied to the concave root-quantile with the Beta(d,1) rank law, whose mean is d/(d+1).

The cone-profile formula treats every tilt: a full endpoint costs at least a; otherwise sharp Holder bounds the two nonnegative support deficits. The full-A, empty-B state is always realizable by sending its deficit arbitrarily high. If the unconstrained objective is below a, neither coordinate can reach its upper cutoff, so its equality point is a genuine proper-cut realization. The one-dimensional linear case and m=0,1 endpoints are separately covered.

The explicit planar source failure has exact fibers A,K,B because A is contained in K=B. Its chosen mixed point is the prescribed weighted centroid, not the unequal-volume true centroid. The ambient halfspace captures all A, one proper K cap and only the null B apex. The printed rational area and positive deficit agree with independent root Fraction arithmetic. It refutes that source choice, not OC.

The stronger projected-density statement is also valid nonsmoothly. On compact interior intervals the root density and the quantile maps are locally Lipschitz, so the chain identities hold almost everywhere and preserve null exceptional sets. The derivatives in rank and physical coordinates differ by exactly (p+1)/p. A nonincreasing derivative representative integrates to concavity in both directions. The negative-power mean is coordinatewise increasing with exactly the printed negative-semidefinite rank-one Hessian. Its composition with concave rank functions therefore proves the new projected root concavity without smoothing or a multidimensional displacement claim.

Finally, Section 6 gives a uniform actual obstruction for every d>=2. The height formula has the correct simplex centroid coefficient. Under epsilon<=1/(10d), g<1/2, ensuring the stated all-A/null-B statuses. The twice-integrated quadratic bound for 1-(1-s)^d has the correct inequality sign. Its successive relaxations yield Gamma_d[d+77/200]-1 after division by a. This is 3/50 for d=2 and greater than 77/600 for d>=3. All factors and dimension bounds are exact. The stronger directional shape properties do not repair this prescribed center, so a successful use must retain actual relocation or another source.

None of these directional or source-calibration statements is a full arbitrary-body, arbitrary-rank OC theorem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
